execution_policy.numerical_jobs: one at a time, two native threads per process (OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/VECLIB_MAXIMUM/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=2), fresh process per run where the driver does so
execution_policy.guard: shwfs_ao.runtime.resource_guard: policy budget min(2 GiB, 12.5 % physical, 25 % available), 2x margin on the audited raw peak, 64 MiB scratch ceiling, refusal on warn/critical memory pressure; an authorized budget above the policy only through tools/authorized_supervise.py with a written note
execution_policy.series_identity: one producing host, one locked environment, one code identity per series; no resume across hosts, environments or code; historical records are never relabelled
execution_policy.enablement: governed commands run only with --enabled-by-user '<YYYY-MM-DD: the user's wording>' supplied by the user for that concrete run; earlier instructions to ignore the guard are not inherited
execution_policy.cloud_session: commands capped at 150 min each; stages run as chained background invocations with --timeout-s at most 8400 s and the drivers' resume; records pushed or copied out before the session ends
